response.sql:
WITH project_spatial AS (
  SELECT 
    p.fundflux,
    ss.boxx,
    ss.boxy,
    ss.aream2,
    ss.volm3
  FROM projects p
  JOIN scanspatial ss ON p.arcregistry = ss.arcref
),
funding_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    fundflux,
    AVG(CASE WHEN boxx IS NOT NULL AND boxx != 0 AND boxy IS NOT NULL 
              THEN (boxy - boxx) / boxx ELSE NULL END) as avg_y_vs_x,
    AVG(CASE WHEN volm3 IS NOT NULL AND volm3 != 0 AND aream2 IS NOT NULL 
              THEN aream2 / volm3 ELSE NULL END) as avg_area_to_vol
  FROM project_spatial
  GROUP BY fundflux
),
cross_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_area_to_vol) as overall_avg
  FROM funding_metrics
)
SELECT 
  fm.fundflux,
  fm.avg_y_vs_x,
  fm.avg_area_to_vol,
  fm.avg_area_to_vol - ca.overall_avg as above_average
FROM funding_metrics fm
CROSS JOIN cross_avg ca
WHERE fm.avg_area_to_vol > ca.overall_avg
ORDER BY fm.fundflux;

assumptions.assumption: "Ignore missing values" means calculate each metric only from spatial records where the relevant values are non-NULL and non-zero (for denominators). Records with missing values for one metric are still included in calculations for the other metric if they have valid data.

The cross-source average of area-to-volume figures is computed from all funding sources in the result set (those with valid avg_area_to_vol values); funding sources with no spatial records contribute NULL and are excluded from the average by SQL's AVG function.

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignore missing values" could mean: exclude any spatial record that has a missing value for either metric from both calculations, rather than treating each metric independently. This would reduce the sample size for both averages if a record lacks data for either metric.

WITH project_spatial AS (
  SELECT 
    p.fundflux,
    ss.boxx,
    ss.boxy,
    ss.aream2,
    ss.volm3
  FROM projects p
  JOIN scanspatial ss ON p.arcregistry = ss.arcref
  WHERE ss.boxx IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxx != 0 AND ss.boxy IS NOT NULL
    AND ss.aream2 IS NOT NULL AND ss.volm3 IS NOT NULL AND ss.volm3 != 0
),
funding_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    fundflux,
    AVG((boxy - boxx) / boxx) as avg_y_vs_x,
    AVG(aream2 / volm3) as avg_area_to_vol
  FROM project_spatial
  GROUP BY fundflux
),
cross_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_area_to_vol) as overall_avg
  FROM funding_metrics
)
SELECT 
  fm.fundflux,
  fm.avg_y_vs_x,
  fm.avg_area_to_vol,
  fm.avg_area_to_vol - ca.overall_avg as above_average
FROM funding_metrics fm
CROSS JOIN cross_avg ca
WHERE fm.avg_area_to_vol > ca.overall_avg
ORDER BY fm.fundflux;
